item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0008-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0008-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0008-E003","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0008-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0008-E005","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The UN Working Group’s September 2023 Mexico visit identified positive legal institutions, including the National Detention Registry and the torture-prevention mechanism, but found arbitrary detention widespread, citing preventive detention, arraigo, militarized security, excessive force, weak legal assistance, attacks on judicial independence, poor detention conditions, and particular impacts on Indigenous people; it also raised concerns about frequent detention of migrants.","notes":["The excerpt specifically identifies particular effects on Indigenous people and separately expresses concern about frequent migrant detention; it does not state that migrants experienced particular impacts in the same sense."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0008-E006","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0008-E007","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0008-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0008-E009","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"A 2023 human-rights and legal study stated that the López Obrador administration had been repeatedly criticized by civil associations over corruption concerns, opaque public-resource management, excessive public-works spending, and an authoritarian determination in applying those policies; it stated that the transparency institution had been paralyzed since 2022 and included bibliography references to reporting on transparency, staffing, information denials, and noncompetitive procurement.","notes":["The supplied excerpt is an abstract and bibliography; it does not itself present detailed empirical findings establishing reduced staffing, increased denials, or noncompetitive procurement."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0008-E010","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"WOLA reported in September 2023 that Sedena did not register its arrests in the legally required National Detention Registry, that military detention statistics appeared significantly underreported, and that authorities had concealed Ayotzinapa information and used Pegasus against activists; it also cited abuses by federal forces and the National Guard, alleged crime-scene alteration, and stated that impunity remained the norm.","notes":["The excerpt says that impunity remains the norm; the narrower wording tracks the source exactly."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0008-E011","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0008-E012","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"López Obrador accused elite journalists of sabotaging his government, alleged that Carlos Loret de Mola’s income came from corruption, asked INAI to investigate and disclose the journalist’s income and assets, and said opposition and free expression were legitimate while describing Loret and an elite or mercenary press as linked to corruption and political interests.","notes":["The excerpt supports allegations about Loret and an elite or mercenary press, but does not specifically establish that associated media were corrupt political actors."]}]}
